en: The Apadāna of the Elder Udakadāyaka Kaṇikārapupphiyavagga, Chapter 6 I was a merchant in Benares, and I gave a gift of water to the Buddha Vipassī, who was weary from his journey. Because of that deed, I have been reborn in heaven for eighty-four thousand aeons. Having passed through those existences, I was born here in this world as a human being. Having abandoned the five lower fetters, I am now an Anāgāmī, one who will not return to this world again. My life span is long, my strength is great, and my complexion is exceedingly beautiful. I dwell in the forest, free from fear, having attained the state of an Anāgāmī. I shall pass away from this world and go to the Brahma realm; there I shall dwell until the end of the aeon. This is the fruit of giving water to the Buddha. Thus, by means of this small gift, I have attained such a state. May all beings be happy and well. May they be free from suffering. “Seeing a monk eating,
with a mind serene and unperturbed,
one should take water in a jar.”
I gave [it] to Siddhattha.
Today I am stainless,
pure, and my doubts are destroyed.
When a new existence was being produced,
my fruit was produced.
Ninety-four aeons ago,
I have been a servant of Yama;
yet I do not recognize an evil rebirth—
this is the fruit of the gift of water.
In the sixty-first aeon,
there was but one Vimala,
who was endowed with the seven treasures.
A wheel-turning monarch of great power.
The four analytical knowledges... [and so forth]...
“Such is the teaching of the Buddha.
Thus indeed did the venerable elder Udakadāyaka recite these verses.
This is the sixth legend of the elder Udakadāyaka.
